answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent network can anchor identities to optical physical unclonable functions. A randomness beacon issues unpredictable challenges, prompting each node to illuminate a disordered willow cellulose token with a calibrated violet laser. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of fabricating discrete, non-cloneable physical scattering keys per identity. However, thermal drift and minor vibrations alter diffraction paths, causing false rejections.
